canonical_statement: The analysis evaluated whether the TIMI heparin nomogram achieved and maintained therapeutic anticoagulation and assessed its safety after thrombolytic therapy for acute myocardial infarction.
Eligible TIMI 4 participants were men or women younger than 80 years with ischemic chest pain lasting more than 30 minutes who presented within 6 hours of chest-pain onset.

population.label: TIMI 4 acute myocardial infarction population
inclusion_criteria: Presentation within 6 hours of chest-pain onset

canonical_statement: Eligible participants had ST-segment elevation greater than 0.1 mV in two contiguous leads or a new left bundle-branch block.

population.label: TIMI 4 acute myocardial infarction population
inclusion_criteria: ST elevation >0.1 mV in two contiguous leads or new left bundle-branch block

canonical_statement: Patients with standard contraindications to thrombolysis were excluded.
One randomized TIMI 4 thrombolytic regimen was front-loaded weight-adjusted alteplase: 15 mg IV bolus, 0.75 mg/kg over 30 minutes, then 0.5 mg/kg over 60 minutes, with a maximum total dose of 100 mg.

exposures.details: 15 mg bolus, then 0.75 mg/kg over 30 min, then 0.5 mg/kg over 60 min; maximum total dose 100 mg

canonical_statement: One randomized TIMI 4 thrombolytic regimen was anistreplase (APSAC) 30 U as a bolus.
The combination thrombolytic regimen used alteplase 15 mg IV bolus followed by 0.75 mg/kg over 30 minutes (maximum 65 mg) plus anistreplase 20 U as a bolus.

exposures.details: 15 mg bolus then 0.75 mg/kg over 30 min; maximum 65 mg

canonical_statement: Aspirin 325 mg was given at study entry and daily thereafter.

exposures.details: Given at study entry and daily thereafter

canonical_statement: Intravenous heparin was started immediately at study entry with a 5000-U bolus followed by a 1000-U/h infusion and was continued for 4 days unless contraindicated.
aPTT was scheduled at 8, 12, and 24 hours after heparin initiation and daily thereafter.
After a change in heparin dosage, aPTT was checked 6 to 8 hours later.
aPTT was additionally checked if reinfarction or bleeding occurred.
The heparin nomogram targeted an aPTT of 1.5 to 2 times the control value.

outcome.definition: aPTT 1.5 to 2 times the control value

canonical_statement: For aPTT at least 3 times control, the suggested nomogram decreased the heparin infusion by 50%.

exposures.details: Decrease infusion by 50% when aPTT >=3x control

canonical_statement: For aPTT 2 to 3 times control, the suggested nomogram decreased the heparin infusion by 25%.

exposures.details: Decrease infusion by 25% when aPTT 2-3x control

canonical_statement: For aPTT 1.5 to 2 times control, the suggested nomogram made no change to the heparin infusion.
For aPTT below 1.5 times control, the suggested nomogram increased the heparin infusion by 25%, with a maximum rate of 2500 U/h.

exposures.details: Increase infusion by 25% when aPTT <1.5x control; maximum rate 2500 U/h

canonical_statement: For arterial-sheath removal, the heparin infusion was reduced by half for 4 hours before sheath removal and resumed at the previous rate 4 hours after removal.
Reocclusion was defined as TIMI flow grade 2 or 3 at 90 minutes after thrombolytic initiation followed by TIMI flow grade 0 or 1 at follow-up catheterization 18 to 36 hours later.

outcome.definition: Initially patent vessel (TIMI flow 2 or 3 at 90 min) with subsequent TIMI flow 0 or 1 at follow-up angiography 18-36 h later

canonical_statement: Reinfarction surveillance used ischemic pain plus standard electrocardiographic and enzyme criteria.

outcome.definition: Ischemic pain plus standard electrocardiographic and enzyme criteria

canonical_statement: Differences between proportions were tested with chi-square analyses and differences between means with t tests; all P values were two-tailed and P<0.05 was considered significant.
The interim analysis included the first 217 TIMI 4 participants: 158 men and 59 women.
The mean age of the 217 participants was 58.0 years with an SD of 10.9 years.
The median aPTT at 8 hours after thrombolytic therapy was 120 seconds.

canonical_statement: At 24 hours, patients with subtherapeutic aPTT values were younger than those with therapeutic values (55.2±10.6 vs 59.6±10.6 years; P=.02); the calculated mean difference was -4.4 years.
At 24 hours, patients with subtherapeutic aPTT values weighed more than those with therapeutic values (86.4±13.5 vs 78.9±15.7 kg; P=.007); the calculated mean difference was 7.5 kg.

Nine participating centers used the recommended heparin nomogram and six centers used local heparin-adjustment practice; nomogram use was identified by a center poll rather than randomized assignment.
Centers using the recommended heparin nomogram had significantly fewer subtherapeutic aPTT values at 48 and 96 hours than centers using local practice.

Within 96 hours, heparin therapy was interrupted in 45 of 118 patients (38.1%) at nomogram centers versus 68 of 99 patients (68.7%) at non-nomogram centers (P<.001); the calculated risk difference was -30.6 percentage points.

canonical_statement: The small numbers of reinfarction and reocclusion events prevented a valid statistical comparison between nomogram and non-nomogram groups.
Use of the heparin nomogram was not randomly assigned to centers, so factors other than nomogram use could account for observed between-center differences.
Even at centers using the nomogram, a large percentage of patients remained in the subtherapeutic aPTT range.
The authors suggested that future nomograms should consider weight-adjusted heparin dosing because patients with subtherapeutic 24-hour aPTT values weighed more.
The authors suggested that different heparin nomograms might be needed for different age categories because anticoagulation was more difficult in younger patients.

The authors proposed that more frequent monitoring for low aPTT values, potentially every 6 hours with appropriate infusion-rate increases, might improve therapeutic anticoagulation during the first 24 hours.
The authors concluded that a standardized heparin nomogram appeared useful for improving anticoagulation after thrombolytic therapy for acute myocardial infarction.
The authors concluded that very frequent aPTT monitoring and a standardized approach to heparin dose adjustment were supported by their findings.
